acquisition_method.evidence: Data was acquired in data-dependent mode, and the top 7 most abundant precursors were acquired each duty cycle.

alkylation_concentration.evidence: Specifically, lysates were thawed at room temperature, and proteins reduced and alkylated using 5 mM chloroacetamide and 5 mM Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine.

alkylation_reagent.evidence: Specifically, lysates were thawed at room temperature, and proteins reduced and alkylated using 5 mM chloroacetamide and 5 mM Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine.

cleavage_agent.evidence: An initial round of digestion was performed using 1:200 enzyme-to-protein ratio of endoproteinase Lys-C (Wako), overnight at room temperature.
Subsequently, second-stage digestion was performed using 150 ng of Endoproteinase Asp-N (Roche), overnight at 30°C, mixing at 300 rpm.

collision_energy.evidence: Precursors from a range of 550–1500 m/z and with charge states 2–6 were selected using an isolation width of 1.3 m/z, and fragmented using higher-energy collision dissociation with normalized collision energy of 25.

enrichment_method.evidence: Six hundred microliters of Protein G Agarose beads (Roche) were used to immobilize 100 μl of SUMO-2/3 antibody (8A2, acquired from Abcam, ab81371; ∼5–10-μg/μl antibody).

fragmentation_method.evidence: Precursors from a range of 550–1500 m/z and with charge states 2–6 were selected using an isolation width of 1.3 m/z, and fragmented using higher-energy collision dissociation with normalized collision energy of 25.

ionization_type.evidence: ionization was achieved using a NanoSpray Flex™ NG ion source (Thermo).

ptm.evidence: Variable modifications used were protein N-terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation, peptide N-terminal pyroglutamate, Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphorylation (STY), and Lys sumoylation, with a maximum of three modifications per peptide.
